bug_semantics: SubjectX500PrincipalExtractor turns an X.509 client certificate's X500Principal into an RFC2253 (CN) or RFC1779 (email OID) DN string and takes matcher.find() group(1) from the regex CN=(.*?)(?:,|$) or OID.1.2.840.113549.1.9.1=(.*?)(?:,|$). Because the regex is unanchored and stops at the first CN=/OID= substring, a CN or OU value that embeds a second DN-like fragment (for example OU=CN=duke,) is parsed as that other username. A crafted client certificate can therefore impersonate another user in X.509 pre-authentication. The vendor advisory and CVE.org record keep this as a real published issue affecting Spring Security 7.0.0–7.0.4 (CWE-297); exploitation assumes the cert already passed a trusted upstream.
flaw_origin: The regex-on-stringified-DN extractor was first written when SubjectX500PrincipalExtractor was added and made the default X509AuthenticationFilter extractor. That commit copied the historical CN=(.*?)(?:,|$) approach onto X500Principal.getName() output rather than parsing RDNs. A later encapsulate commit only moved the same patterns to static fields; it did not invent the match-first-CN behavior. The 7.0.5 fix replaces the regex with javax.naming.ldap.LdapName/Rdn iteration so an embedded CN= inside another RDN is no longer treated as the subject.

reasoning: CVE-2026-22747 is a published VMware/Spring advisory, not withdrawn: SubjectX500PrincipalExtractor mis-parses malformed certificate CN/email DN strings and can bind the wrong username. The vulnerable mechanism is unanchored regex extraction against X500Principal.getName() output. git log -L/-S and parent-tree checks place the first write of those lines at aba437d4698c0b30559021e3f41b85607fee8ce0, which also made the new class the default extractor; the parent e8f920e0eeafff1af55427c13db054a3b6b13830 has neither the file nor the class name. The deprecated SubjectDnX509PrincipalExtractor already used a similar CN regex on getSubjectDN(), but that is a different class/DN source, was left unpatched by this CVE, and is absent from 7.0.0–7.0.4 scope; aba437d is a new-file first-write, not a move. Encapsulate commit f690a7f is a refactor of the same patterns. The GHSA fix 88118afb8f9357ae7cc215500a441e89fee701c3 is the direct RDN-parsing patch, present in 7.0.5 and not 7.0.4, matching the vendor boundary.
